# Linux embedded Python

This directory builds CPython 2.3.4 and the vendored zlib 1.2.3 as
`libdice_py.so` for Linux x86-64. It supports a standalone interpreter check and
the root engine build. See the public
[build guide](../../../../../docs/building.md#linux-and-wsl) for the engine targets.

## Build and check

From the repository root on Linux or WSL, with CMake 3.21 or newer, Ninja, and
GCC or Clang:

```sh
cmake -S Code/BF2/External/python-embedded/linux -B "$HOME/bf2py-build" \
      -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build "$HOME/bf2py-build" --target dice_py dice_py_check
cmake --build "$HOME/bf2py-build" --target dice_py_check_run
```

Under WSL, keep the build directory in the Linux filesystem. The standalone
output directory defaults to `<build>/bin_linux`; `BF2_DICE_PY_OUTPUT_DIR` can
override it. The root project places the library beside `bf2`. The executable
and check use an `$ORIGIN` runtime search path.

| Target | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dice_py` | Build `libdice_py.so` |
| `dice_py_check` | Build the C++14 interpreter-check executable |
| `dice_py_check_lib` | Stage `copy_reg.py` and `types.py` in the build tree |
| `dice_py_check_run` | Run the check with those staged modules |

The check verifies interpreter initialization/finalization, pointer and data
exports, builtin imports, a zlib roundtrip, and loopback UDP send/receive. It
binds an ephemeral port and rejects 16567. It does not exercise compressed
standard-library ZIP imports, dynamic extension loading, or the game's boot
path. Prefix-search and deprecated-module warnings may appear during this
isolated check.

Staged modules and their generated bytecode live under
`<build>/dice_py/check/lib`, keeping the vendored `Lib/` directory clean.

## Build contracts

[CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt) derives its source list from
[pythoncore.files](../../../../Build/python/pythoncore.files). It replaces the
Windows module table, path discovery, and dynamic loader with Unix equivalents.
The Linux table uses `posix` instead of `nt` and omits `msvcrt`.
The 64-bit build also excludes `audioop`, `imageop`, `rgbimg`, and
`yuvconvert`, following the upstream 64-bit exclusions.

Zlib is mandatory because compressed ZIP imports need it. The shared library
links with `--no-undefined`; its system dependencies include threads, dynamic
loading, math, and `libutil` when `openpty` is not supplied by libc.

Preserve the GNU C90 dialect, `-fno-strict-aliasing`, `-fwrapv`, PIC, and default
symbol visibility. The target fixes `-O2 -g` and defines `Py_BUILD_CORE`,
`NDEBUG`, and `BF2_HAVE_ZLIB`. Both the library and check define `DEDICATED=1`
and force-include the engine's `BuildConfig.h`. Compiler-specific tolerance flags
are tested before use.

## Configuration and local changes

The checked-in [pyconfig.h](pyconfig.h) targets little-endian Linux x86-64 with
LP64 types, 16-byte `fpos_t`, UCS-2 Unicode, threads, and pymalloc. CMake rejects
other architectures. This configuration is not a portable replacement for a
fresh configure result on another ABI.

To regenerate it, copy the vendored source to an empty scratch directory and run
`CC='gcc -std=gnu89' ./configure` there. The older configure probes require that
dialect on current GCC; using its default can misdetect type sizes and platform
features. Review the resulting header before installing it here. Do not run
configure in the vendored source tree.

The build deliberately reports `sys.platform` as `linux2`. Its path-discovery
defaults use Python 2.3 under `/usr/local` with an empty `VPATH`; the engine
sets its game-content paths after interpreter initialization.

The vendored interpreter has a local LP64 correction in
[Modules/zipimport.c](../py-src-2.3.4/Modules/zipimport.c):
`PyObject_CallFunction(decompress, "Oi", raw_data, -15)` uses `i` for the
`int` argument. The previous `l` format expected a wider `long` on LP64 and
could make compressed ZIP imports fail with `OverflowError`. Preserve this
patch when updating the source; the vendored tree is not byte-identical to its
upstream release.

Keep the [upstream Python license](../py-src-2.3.4/LICENSE) and source notices
with the interpreter.
